source.title: Evaluating Open-Source Sparse Autoencoders on Disentangling Factual Knowledge in GPT-2 Small

page_placements.theme: Native neurons match or beat dictionary features on some tests, and much dictionary activity duplicates single MLP neurons

record.tranche_reason: The study uses interchange interventions to evaluate neurons as causal feature units for separating factual knowledge, rather than testing neuron-pole job counts or attribution graphs.
record.gate_note: The paper tests neuron features against SAE features and a DAS skyline on city-country and city-continent knowledge. It does not test neuron-pole interpretability shares, explanation scoring on unseen activations, or attribution graphs. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: No version is tested. The study compares feature bases (residual-stream dimensions, four SAEs, DAS) as causal mediators of city-country and city-continent knowledge in GPT-2 small. Its 'neurons' are residual-stream basis dimensions, not MLP neuron poles. It reports no job shares (V1/V2), no vision neurons (V3/V4), no attribution graphs explaining behaviour (V5), and no explanation scoring (V6/V7). The neuron-vs-DAS gap and the SAE reconstruction damage are related but different constructs, recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors find the Bloom and Apollo SAEs below the neuron baseline and the OpenAI top-k SAE only matching it (~70). None approaches the DAS skyline (~95). SAE reconstructions degrade GPT-2's city knowledge. The neuron–DAS gap shows polysemantic dimensions that can be improved upon.
record.recipe_differences: Uses learned binary masks and interchange interventions on GPT-2 small neuron features to test factual-knowledge separation; it is not a neuron-pole audit or attribution-graph evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: Layer and intervention target; Apollo SAEs were available only at layers 1, 5, and 9.

fits_no_version.finding: In GPT-2 small, the residual-stream basis (layers 1 and 5) separates country from continent knowledge with disentangle scores of 71–73. A rotated DAS basis reaches 94–96. The authors read this as evidence of polysemantic dimensions needing rotation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The native residual-stream basis of a language model localizes related factual attributes markedly worse than a supervised rotated basis.

fits_no_version.finding: No SAE beats the neuron basis at disentangling. Bloom and Apollo fall below it, and OpenAI top-k only matches it (~70). Substituting SAE reconstructions degrades city knowledge: OpenAI at layer 1 keeps 95, while Apollo e2e+ds keeps 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Public SAEs for GPT-2 small do not provide better causal mediators than the native basis, and their reconstruction error costs model knowledge.

record.problems: The evaluation is limited to GPT-2 small, 40 cities, and country/continent facts; the authors describe the dataset as i.i.d. to give SAEs a favorable evaluation. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 1a's layer-by-layer curves and layerwise details beyond layers 1 and 5, plus detailed country/continent accuracy values for comparator feature spaces, were not extracted; the retained rows prioritize neuron results and the principal disentangle-score comparisons. Reconstruction and sparsity results concern SAE representations rather than the neuron-unit claim.

untested.parts: All: no neuron-pole audit or job shares in Qwen3-32B.
All: no interpretability shares in any model; only GPT-2 small is used.
All: no vision neurons, no InceptionV1, no pose or recursive generalization.
All: no architecture or tool comparison of neuron interpretability shares.
All: no attribution graphs built from neurons, and no behaviour explained by them. The 'neurons' here are residual-stream dimensions.
All: no neuron explanations checked against where neurons fire.
All: no simulation-based scoring of explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The study's 'neurons' are residual-stream coordinates above the city token, not MLP neurons. Several layer 5 comparator values were swapped between Bloom and Apollo e2e. The column order is confirmed by matching the reconstruction losses to Table 1. The reader's V5 link and limits_scope label are removed: the study has no attribution graphs or behaviour explanation.

versions.untested_parts: Neuron-pole counts and the shares with one job, two related jobs, or not-yet-understood jobs.
Other language models, model scale, dense versus MoE architecture, and trillion-parameter models.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons, pose detection, and recursive generalization versus superposition.
Architecture or tools as the cause of interpretability differences, and the stated InceptionV1-sized model estimates.

Attribution graphs, explaining model behaviour with such graphs, and comparison to a trained replacement model or its reconstruction error. The study tests neuron features for causal localization of factual knowledge using interchange interventions.
Whether explanations derived from activating examples predict where neurons fire.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulated activations on new text.

relation.reason: It discusses polysemantic 'neurons', which here are residual-stream dimensions, as a baseline. It neither tests nor uses the neurons-already-clean claim.

tranche.reason: The study compares residual-stream basis dimensions, four SAEs and DAS as causal mediators of city knowledge in GPT-2 small. It tests no version: there is no neuron-pole audit share, no other-model share, no InceptionV1, no attribution graphs, and no explanation scoring.

source_check.notes: The 'neurons' are residual-stream basis dimensions above the city token, not MLP neurons. Figure 1c is flattened. Reconstruction losses (644/937/2383/2353, Table 1) fix the layer 5 column order as OpenAI, Bloom, Apollo e2e, Apollo e2e+ds, so Bloom is 64 and both Apollo SAEs are 44. The neuron baseline is 71 at layer 1 and 73 at layer 5 (country-intervened). At layer 1, OpenAI's 73 is numerically 2 above the neuron baseline, but the authors call it a match.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GPT-2 small, residual stream above the city token, layers 1 and 5, RAVEL city-country/continent test
reader_labels.reason: Neuron interventions yielded disentangle scores of 71–73, below the DAS scores of 94–96; neurons served as a useful baseline but did not fully separate these facts (r3, r6, r9, r12, r13, r18, r23, r28). The study does not test attribution graphs.
